reuse.why: The new Fintegra link reuses findOrCreateBank, bankSync.syncAccount and handleSyncResponse, but the take-over path rewrites unlinkAccount's field reset instead of sharing it, and the provider link/download bodies are copied rather than factored.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount repeats the ~60-line upgrade-or-create/sync/notify body of the other five link functions, downloadFintegraTransactions repeats the Akahu/Enable Banking download body, and the replace branch repeats unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount reset block.

placement.why: The link guards live in accounts/link.ts beside findOrCreateBank, the download in sync.ts and the URL in server-config, matching the tree's layering, though a side-effecting unlink inside an 'ensure' guard is an odd home.

scope.why: Edits are limited to the guards, the provider wiring, the new type and the tests the steps require.

maintainability.why: Shared guards are a good start, but every link function must remember two separate guard calls, ensureAccountIsNotLinked silently mutates another account when a flag is set, and a sixth copy of the link flow raises the cost of future link rules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: link.ts ensureAccountIsNotLinked resets bank/account_id/sync fields with its own db.updateAccount copy instead of a shared unlink helper used by unlinkAccount (app.ts)

abstraction_drift.where: link.ts ensureAccountIsNotLinked gains the replaceExistingLink flag and an in-helper branch that unlinks the other account instead of throwing; all six link functions call the guards
